wiki_text: In November 2025 Venture Global filed a FERC application (and a corresponding DOE export application) for the Plaquemines LNG brownfield expansion, scaling the project up roughly 40% from its March 2025 announcement. As filed, the expansion comprises 32 modular liquefaction trains built incrementally in three phases, adding more than 30.0 mtpa of peak production capacity and taking the entire Plaquemines complex to more than 58 mtpa peak. In March 2026 the DOE separately granted a 13% increase (0.45 Bcf/d) in non-FTA export volume, raising Plaquemines' total permitted exports to 3.85 Bcf/d. (GEM models this expansion as the 'Expansion (T37-60)' unit with an inferred baseload of 17.78 mtpa; the 30+ mtpa figure above is peak, not nameplate.)
source_notes: Nov 2025 FERC filing / 32 trains / 3 phases / >30 mtpa peak / >58 mtpa total / ~40% upsizing corroborated by two independent trade-press outlets: LNG Industry (token '58' PASS) and Oil & Gas Journal (token '32' PASS). March 2026 DOE 13% / 0.45 Bcf/d / 3.85 Bcf/d non-FTA increase corroborated by DOE primary (energy.gov, token '3.85' PASS) and WorkBoat (token '3.85' PASS). The prior Venture Global IR and BusinessWire citations were dropped (sponsor primary + its own press echo are not independent, and both 403'd the verifier). Removed the FERC 'authorize by June 25, 2026' sentence: not independently re-corroborated this pass.

topic: FERC draft EIS for Stage 5 expansion (April 2026)
wiki_text: On April 6, 2026 FERC issued a draft environmental impact statement for Cheniere's Sabine Pass Stage 5 expansion (Trains 7-9, ~20 mtpa total across two phases, with Phase 1 Train 7 at ~6 mtpa), with a public comment period running to May 26, 2026. In May 2026 Cheniere Partners signed a lump-sum turnkey EPC contract with Bechtel (~$4.69 billion) for the first phase and issued a limited notice to proceed with early engineering and procurement, targeting a final investment decision on Phase 1 by early 2027; the FERC and DOE applications remained pending.
source_notes: Draft EIS / April 2026 / Train 7-9 / comment period to May 26, 2026 corroborated by LNG Prime (tokens 'May 26' and 'Train 7' PASS) and the Federal Register notice of availability (DOE/FERC primary, token 'May 26' PASS) — two independent sources. The Bechtel EPC contract / ~$4.69B / limited notice to proceed / early-2027 Phase 1 FID corroborated by Natural Gas Intelligence (token 'Bechtel' PASS) and Oil & Gas Journal (token 'Bechtel' PASS) — two independent sources. wiki_text revised to reflect the May 2026 EPC signing (the prior 'finalized a construction agreement, FID in 2027, first LNG 2030' wording was tightened to what these sources state).
